_what: Dog born-as long-form, written to the lion v2 structure and Social Studio's 11/15 long-form rule from the start: promise by 0:05, no rules or score intro, no silent countdowns, a timed shot every 2 to 4 s (test), one mid-video pick-a-number comment prompt, citations on screen (source_tag) and in the description only. Facts: /workspace/drafts/facts/dog-bornas.md (DB1 to DB37).
titles: Your Life as a Dog: 8 Things You Have to Get Through
_titles_note: Title from the brief. MASTER_ORDERS, posted.csv and the topic CSV name no dog title, so nothing overrides it. Single title, no A/B set.

description:
What is life like for a dog? This is your whole life as one, from eyes shut in a litter of about five to a grey muzzle: 8 things you have to get through, then the verdict. Meatball tried all eight at home, with his dog, Noodle, as the real dog and his cat, Sauce, as everybody else.

Checked facts in this video:
- Puppies are born with their eyes and ears closed; they open at about 13 to 19 days (Merck Veterinary Manual).
- In Norwegian purebred records, 8% of puppies died before 8 days old (Tønnessen et al. 2012).
- Behavior problems are the number one reason dogs are given up to shelters (AVSAB).
- Parvovirus: puppies under 4 months and dogs not fully vaccinated are at increased risk. If your puppy shows signs (no appetite, vomiting, fever, severe or bloody diarrhea), call your veterinarian right away (AVMA).
- Chocolate is toxic to dogs; theobromine can cause mild signs at doses as low as 9 mg per pound of body weight (FDA).
- Xylitol can drop a dog's blood sugar within 10 to 60 minutes. If you think your dog ate xylitol, chocolate, grapes, raisins, onions or garlic, note how much and call your vet, an emergency clinic, or animal poison control right away (FDA, ASPCA). ASPCA Animal Poison Control: (888) 426-4435.
- Never leave a dog alone in a parked car, no matter the outdoor temperature or how long you'll be gone. A car can rise about 20°F in 10 minutes (AVMA).
- Overweight dogs had a shorter median life in all 12 breeds studied (Salt et al. 2019).
- Dogs don't age 7 human years per dog year (AVMA).

General information, not veterinary advice. Ask your vet about your own dog.

Sources:
- Merck Veterinary Manual, Social Behavior of Dogs: https://www.merckvetmanual.com/behavior/behavior-of-dogs/social-behavior-of-dogs ; Canine Parvovirus Infection: https://www.merckvetmanual.com/digestive-system/infectious-diseases-of-the-gastrointestinal-tract-in-small-animals/canine-parvovirus-infection-parvoviral-enteritis-in-dogs
- Merck Veterinary Manual (dog owners), Normal Social Behavior in Dogs: https://www.merckvetmanual.com/dog-owners/behavior-of-dogs/normal-social-behavior-in-dogs
- Borge KS, Tønnessen R, Nødtvedt A, Indrebø A (2011) Litter size at birth in purebred dogs: a retrospective study of 224 breeds. Theriogenology 75:911-919. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21196028/
- Tønnessen R, Borge KS, Nødtvedt A, Indrebø A (2012) Canine perinatal mortality: a cohort study of 224 breeds. Theriogenology 77:1788-1801. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22365700/
- American Veterinary Society of Animal Behavior, Position Statement on Puppy Socialization: https://avsab.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/Puppy-Socialization-Position-Statement-FINAL.pdf
- AVMA: Canine parvovirus brochure https://ebusiness.avma.org/files/productdownloads/MCM-ClientBrochures-20-CanineParvovirus.pdf ; Pet safety in vehicles https://www.avma.org/resources-tools/pet-owners/petcare/pets-vehicles ; Pet dental care https://www.avma.org/resources-tools/pet-owners/petcare/pet-dental-care ; Senior pets https://www.avma.org/resources-tools/pet-owners/petcare/senior-pets
- ASPCA, Pet Statistics (2025 shelter estimates): https://www.aspca.org/helping-people-pets/shelter-intake-and-surrender/pet-statistics ; People Foods to Avoid Feeding Your Pets: https://www.aspca.org/pet-care/aspca-poison-control/people-foods-avoid-feeding-your-pets
- ASPCA Animal Poison Control Center, (888) 426-4435
- FDA, Leave Chocolate Out of Rover's Celebrations: https://www.fda.gov/animal-veterinary/animal-health-literacy/leave-chocolate-out-rovers-celebrations ; Paws Off Xylitol; It's Dangerous for Dogs: https://www.fda.gov/consumers/consumer-updates/paws-xylitol-its-dangerous-dogs
- Kealy RD et al. (2002) Effects of diet restriction on life span and age-related changes in dogs. JAVMA 220:1315-1320. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11991408/
- Salt C et al. (2019) Association between life span and body condition in neutered client-owned dogs. J Vet Intern Med 33:89-99. https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6335446/
- McMillan KM et al. (2024) Longevity of companion dog breeds: those at risk from early death. Scientific Reports 14:531. https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10834484/
- Wang T et al. (2020) Quantitative translation of dog-to-human aging by conserved remodeling of the DNA methylome. Cell Systems 11:176-185. https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7484147/
- American Kennel Club, Why Does My Dog Sniff Everything?: https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/training/why-does-my-dog-sniff-everything/
- Nagasawa M et al. (2015) Oxytocin-gaze positive loop and the coevolution of human-dog bonds. Science 348:333-336. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25883356/
- Fiset S, Plourde V (2015) Commentary: Oxytocin-gaze positive loop and the coevolution of human-dog bonds. Frontiers in Psychology 6:1845. https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4663257/
- Penn Vet, Dog Body Language Basics: https://www.vet.upenn.edu/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/dogbodylanguagebasics-pdf.pdf
